utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I will rephrase my question, Dr. Gow. Was the city of Gorazde successfully defended by the locals in the early stages of the war of '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the town of Gorazde was one of the areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina in which Muslim or Bosnian government control was maintained throughout that period, although there were periods of fighting in the area, and certainly there were periods in which the fighting -- I will leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I would like to take you to the city of Tuzla. Do you know anything about the composition of the government of those who were in charge of Tuzla? Mayor, the council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know anything about the composition of the local government in Tuzla, although I can report that many people regard it as having been an area of political moderation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the JNA that was in garrison in Tuzla in the early stages of the war? Was there a JNA garrison in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a JNA garrison in Tuzla, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know how many JNA soldiers, officers, were there? Was it a big garrison? Was it a small one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My recollection is that it was a relatively big garrison. A figure -- I do not recall the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What happened to them when the war started, Dr. Gow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure if I understand what you are asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What happened to the JNA? Did they start fighting? Did they leave for Italy? I am asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They certainly did not leave for Italy, as far as I am aware. I do not have specific recollection or knowledge of any detail of what happened but, in general, I think that the units of the JNA there were mostly withdrawn possibly under pressure from -----

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Under pressure from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think under the pressure of mostly under the pressure of circumstances possibly also, well, probably also under the pressure of units of the Bosnian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any negotiation between the local government in Tuzla and the JNA, the JNA being trapped in its garrison, to give them -- I hardly dare to use the word -- a safe conduct out of that city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of that negotiation, but I am aware that negotiations of that kind were taking place in other parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina so, therefore, that would be consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right in assuming that you do not know anything about what happened when this negotiated safe conduct was effected when the JNA left the town, what happened to these JNA people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think you would be right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know of any attack, after having negotiated a way out, leaving to Tuzla, on these JNA personnel leaving the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall anything of that kind now, but again it would be consistent with the events in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, you have talked about setting up crisis committees by the Serbs on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina to prepare for take over of power. Am I using the wrong word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I made reference to something called crisis headquarters, but my recollection is I told you about the provision for crisis headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Where were these crisis headquarters based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Crisis headquarters were to be organised, as far as I recall, in municipalities throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I am mistaken; what I called crisis committees, I refer to what you call crisis headquarters being spread all over -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krizni Stab.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is a word that sounds familiar to me. Were they just Serbian or Serb crisis headquarters, or were they organised as well by the other entities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of crisis headquarters being organised by other parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: You are not aware of a kind of a crisis staff -- whether it has the same name is not essential for me -- a similar organisation of what should be done if a war would break out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you are saying, did other parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina make provision for the running of areas in the event of certain other events, then it is my understanding that some preparation was made, but not preparation of the same kind and of the same nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What was the difference then, Dr. Gow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I am able to express the difference, and my understanding of it may be based on a misunderstanding, the degree to which the Serbian Democratic Party who had made provision and organised throughout the territories of Bosnia and Herzegovina was not necessarily -- sorry, was more extensive and detailed and involved greater collaboration with security service and, indeed, with units of the JNA than similar preparations for which I am aware and about which I have only read on the part of other parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but the fact is still that, according to what I have read, other parties did make preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do I understand you have less knowledge of details of these preparations by the other parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you are talking about the period to which my testimony referred, then I think that would be the correct assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Gow. Are you aware of any other JNA units being trapped in garrisons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where they were trapped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The JNA at its Sarajevo headquarters had difficulties, and in response to that the Commander organised the effective kidnapping of the President of Bosnia and Herzegovina in May when he was returning from a meeting, a European Community meeting, of the Bosnian parties in order to try to secure the exit of the JNA from its garrison in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any other units of the JNA being trapped in their garrisons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have specific recollection of any other specific units being trapped, but again, as had been the case in Croatia, it was a tactic of the non-JNA forces to try to keep JNA forces in its barracks, in the barracks, with the difference between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina that much of the time the JNA had already withdrawn the bulk of its forces from the barracks in Bosnia and Herzegovina, but the tactic remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, we just talked about some paramilitary organisations, were they co-operating with the central government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure again what it is that you are asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. Were there ever meetings of paramilitary organisations together with central government officials in order to establish a common strategy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no specific knowledge of meetings between government officials and members of any paramilitary groups to establish strategy -- is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Establish strategy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To establish military strategy, I am not aware of any specific meetings for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: You are not aware of a meeting in December 1991 where Mr. Itzebegovic met together with paramilitary organisations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware that Mr. Itzebegovic met with members of paramilitary organisations. I am not aware, because such meetings were reported, of the specific content of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: What was then your idea of -- perhaps that is too difficult a question -- of what they were discussing, what Mr. Itzebegovic would discuss with paramilitary organisations? Perhaps I should -----?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I would not mind. I will withdraw that question, your Honour. Dr. Gow, when were you testifying on the several attacks in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you said that these were co-ordinated attacks. Could you please explain exactly what you mean by "co-ordinated" in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, my memory is not that I said "co-ordinated" but if I did say "co-ordinated" then I can maybe characterise it in these terms. There was co-operation, co-ordination between local Serbian political leaders, between elements of the JNA and between certain paramilitary groups. It was part of an overall, in my interpretation, part of an overall programme and, therefore, again would involve elements of co-ordination to establish control in certain locations of some strategic significance in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I did not hear the last part of your answer? Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: No, I mean the part before, the last 10 or 12 words. Perhaps I should look at it. If you do not mind, perhaps I had better look at the transcript and see what I can -- You are just referring perhaps to the maps we discussed yesterday, the maps with the military sites of the air bases. Were there ever any simultaneous attacks on bridges, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure if I can say there were simultaneous attacks on bridges. Certainly a number, at various points a number of bridges along the Sava river had been destroyed and the bridge at Bosanski Brod, I think, was taken control of, if not destroyed, on 27th March. But I am not aware of simultaneous attacks, at least I do not recall any simultaneous attacks now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a great use from a military point of view of destroying one bridge and leave the others, and not simultaneously destroy the other ones as well in the same river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The destruction of bridges would depend on their potential use in the future and need not be simultaneous, but would still be part of a programme of military activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that it was planned, it was co-operation between the JNA and the other groups involved. Could you explain to us if this was a planned action, what exactly was the idea behind this city first, that city, can you give us an explanation on the tactics of what the co-ordination might have been exactly, and perhaps do it by using that same map that we saw yesterday; it was Exhibit 66.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you wish. If I might ----

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: That is not the right one. I have the wrong one as a matter of fact. It is the one with the dates on it of the attacks of the different villages. Whether or not the Registrar is aware?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, can you help us? Maybe 58? I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 57 might be the one, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is 57 your Honour. I am waiting until the Registry has it. Could you explain to me about the systematic aspects of this date and these? You are talking about co-ordination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I think it may be necessary to make it clear that again we are talking about a situation in which there was a degree of ambiguity, in which it would not serve the interests of those pursuing the project to create Serbian territories of which I spoke to carry out a typical and co-ordinated regular attack with regular armed forces. It would not suit them in terms of the type of forces which were available, and it would not suit them in terms of the diplomatic position in which they would find themselves. Therefore, the nature of the attacks spread over a period of a month in part relates to the resources available, the types of forces available and to the need not, as far as possible, not to make what was taking place an explicit activity, so that there would be the possibility of indicating a degree of ambiguity in the situation. Again, I made reference to General Kadijevic with regard to the war in Croatia yesterday, the need in a sense to disguise, to mask, what was actually taking place. The significance of the locations I think I pointed yesterday was that it would control access into and out of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So in the case of the border towns along the Drina, some of which such as Visegrad I think had majority Muslim populations, although again my recollection is no longer secure on that, was to ensure that supplies if necessary would be able to come in and out of Bosnia and Herzegovina to supplement the JNA or other Serbian forces there. You will see Bijeljina, Zvornik and Visegrad all lie on the main routes from Serbia into into Bosnia and Herzegovina, and indeed the main supply route or communications route from Belgrade through to the headquarters of the military established in Bosnia when the second military district moved out of Sarajevo to Ham Pijesak there, approximately there, it is difficult to be sure without clear markings, and followed an order to rename itself the general staff of the VRS in May. The connection between Zvornik Vlasenica is essential for establishing that kind of logistical chain. Similarly, for any forces moving into the southern parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, particularly I have made reference sometimes to the Uzice corps, Uzice is roughly speaking approximately somewhere here in southern Serbia, and again those forces would this axis of communication or supplies which go along that axis of communication into Bosnia and Herzegovina. Opposite, along the northern border, along the River Sava, to the north of here is the Republic of Croatia. It was obviously the case that if border crossing points and major communication points just inside the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina were not to be controlled, were not controlled, then there would be the possibility of Croatian army troops coming in to the northern parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Croatian army troops were present at Bosanski Brod on 27th March -- sorry, they present at Slavonski Brod on the other side of the river 27th March at the time the conflict took pace, that the incidents took place there. The importance in particular of securing Bijeljina and the areas across northern Bosnia is that I think many people are now familiar with what the Serbs regard as the vital strategic corridor across northern Bosnia running from the territory of Serbia through Bijeljina, through the town of the Brcko and the area around it known as the Posavina corridor, and then across northern Bosnia into territory which was controlled by the Serbs through the town of Banja Luka which I think should be there and into the territory occupied in the Dalmatian hinterland by the Croatian Serbs. This would be a vital part of connecting up a set of Serbian territories to which I made reference yesterday and to which General Kadijevic made some reference in his book. Similarly, if you move down here to the town of Kupres which is marked, Kupres is significant because the area here to the south, more or less south of that, was strongly Croatian populated territory. It was the area in which Croatian forces, I mentioned the HOS were present somewhere in that area. Kupres is essential and the Kupres heights running up here are essential for having strategic domination, not only westwards towards the Dalmatian coast but also for the whole of the territory into northern central Bosnia. Therefore, all the places at which these early incidents took place would be part of any sensible strategic plan to establish control of the framework of the situation for any conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I hope in all of that I have managed to answer your question. If I have not I would be happy to try to do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have just one question. You mentioned all of the locations, or certainly most of them, if not by name you have pointed to them. Tell me about Prijedor. You have a date under there of April 30th. Of course the indictment in this case charges acts committed in, allegedly committed in Prijedor. Tell me a little bit more about that, if you will?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My knowledge of Prijedor I would say, I would warn you to begin with ----

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: You have said you have not been there. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- is relatively limited. It appears on the map because in discussions with the Office of the Prosecutor because of the particular case in question, it was thought that the town of Prijedor should be indicated and the date on which Serbian control was established. The takeover of Prijedor itself, as I understand it, was largely bloodless. It involved the presence of armed force but did not involve any significant fighting. That is my understanding, but, as I say, my knowledge of Prijedor itself is very restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: But you do realise that the indictment charges the commission of acts in the Prijedor region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe, again my memory is that I indicated that that was the case and because that was the nature of this particular case, it was in discussion with the Office of the Prosecutor that they asked for Prijedor to be indicated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: So you ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I might just add that Prijedor does again lie on this main axis of communication across northern Bosnia, leading towards the Serbian territories in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Can you tell us then anything about the actions other than what you have already told us around April 30th, and perhaps even continuing through the end of that year? Do you know either from your readings? You have told us that your testimony today is based upon your own readings of other reports. So even though you do not have any first-hand knowledge, obviously, if you have not been there, certainly you have not talked to people there, but you must have read about what occurred in Prijedor and I see it on the map here and it is very relevant to what we are asked to consider. I thought we might get to that. Can you tell the court anything about the actions that occurred in Prijedor on or about April 30th as indicated on exhibit, whatever it is, 57?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before I would go any further in attempting to answer that question, I would say that when I was asked to give assistance to the Office of the Prosecutor in this matter I carried out a limited amount of specific research for this purpose, and at the time using my expertise I was satisfied about certain details and events in the area. This is not work which has formed an integral part of my global understanding of the situation as with the questions earlier about Gorazde. Most of the time I do not have specific micro-detail. I am dealing in my capacity of my work in London more with big pictures, although sometimes I get incidental detail. In that context I would say that although I did some limited specific research on the Prijedor area, I would no longer feel entirely comfortable, particularly in this situation, in saying that although I was satisfied with the work that I did at that point to that stage, I do not think it would be appropriate for me to go much further than that in discussing the case of Prijedor. I can indicate that there was a takeover of Prijedor on 30th April, that there were armed units present, a series of events took place afterwards, and that also in the area, for example, in May there were more violent incidents in villages nearby within the Opstina, but I would not regard myself, I would regard my expert as being broad and general rather than specific in the area of Prijedor. If you wish me to try to go beyond that, I am happy to do so, but I would not in my own judgment think that that would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: If you are not able to, I certainly would not want you. I imagine someone will tell us about Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist in that. It is our intention to call a witness who will specifically address the Prijedor issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, I nevertheless would like to ask you a question on that. You are selecting 11 places on a map and, as far as I understand, you directed the drafting of this map and this map should illustrate a co-ordinated plan of activity. What was the reason why you put Prijedor on it and why you put the 30th April on it, and could you please indicate to us what is the relation as far as the time is concerned of all these places, what exactly explains why Bosanksi Brod was 27th March and Prijedor 30th March, apart from that it is just 32 days in between? Could you please explain to us because you yesterday testified that this explained a lot of things, what does it exactly explain in terms of time, in terms of co-ordinated action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My recollection of the answer I gave a few moments ago in answer to the first part of your question was that the town of Prijedor, I think I gave this in answer to Her Honour Judge McDonald's question, Prijedor in particular was put on the map because in discussion with the Office of the Prosecutor it was decided, I was asked to put it on because it would be useful in the context of the particular case with which you are dealing. The incident at Prijedor, the takeover in Prijedor as far as I can discern did not involve the use, the active use, the use of armed violence, in the same way that the other places I have indicated did, but it would nonetheless fit into the framework that I was trying to explain and to establish, which is that within the first month or so of the armed conflict, that is a week or so or 10 days prior to the international recognition of the independent international personality of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in the remainder of the month following that recognition, that this series of armed actions occurred in these specific locations, and that there is significance in the locations indicated because they would be vital in controlling the strategic nature of any war. The incident at Bosanski Brod on 27th March I believe I already indicated, but I am happy to do so again. I suspect at that time and was the first came specifically because Croatian forces were reported as being present on the other sides of the river, and if the interpretation that I have been giving you is correct, and that there is a need to secure the key entry and exit points into and out of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to try to prevent Croatian forces coming from Slavonski Brod down towards Banja Luka, then that would necessitate the use of armed force at an earlier stage than might otherwise be the case. I think in that context, I am trying to make it very clear, the locations marked are not the only locations where armed incidents took place during this period. For example, significant shelling of Sarajevo was beginning -- they are not only the places in which armed incidents took place, but in the first month of the war there were a series of areas in which broadly similar approaches were used in order to secure important positions in Bosnia and Herzegovina which would be of significance for anybody looking, with a military political strategic perspective for the conduct of any future operations and which would also broadly enable them to form the axes for the territories to form part of the Serbian entity to which again I made reference to in earlier testimony and was identified both as being comprising the Serbian autonomous regions and the type of territories to which I think General Kadijevic made reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, I think I will not pursue this matter, although it is still not clear to me what the co-ordination in time is and it is still not clear to me why you put Prijedor on it, not Sarajevo on it, Prijedor having no, well, not being a part of a military action. But I will just leave it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I indicated that although armed personnel were involved in my understanding at the time of the takeover of Prijedor, violence itself, at least broadly speaking and again other people I am sure will be coming to give more detailed testimony on this, did not -- sorry, any notable level of violence was not used, but I did indicate that although this was put on in part because of the particular case in question and to assist the courts for that purpose, it is also significant that it was within that first month of the conflict and that Prijedor was one of the points on the communication axes across northern Bosnia. I indicated that vital strategic objective in performing an action of this kind would be to secure control of the main communications axes across northern Bosnia and through southern and southwestern Bosnia. I thought that I had said that, but I hope I have been able to make it a little more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, you viewed that the Serbs provoked the conflict in the former Yugoslavia. Is that held because you are biased against the Serbs in your assessment of this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a very difficult question to answer because I am not sure entirely that it is my view that the Serbs provoked the conflict, if that is what you said, but whether or not that is what you said, it is certainly not the case that it reflects a bias of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, an article was given to you. Can you tell me who wrote this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I would tender this article.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want to have a particular number or will it be Defendant's Exhibit 1, A, B?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Bos is in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D1. It will be marked D1 and you have identified it as an article that you have written, Mr. Gow. Mr. Niemann, do you know what the article is?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not know anything about it, your Honour. Could I have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: We have copies. Dr. Gow, I would like to read a few parts of it. The first part, you start this article which is called "Serbian Nationalism and the Hissing Snake in the International Order: Whose Sovereignty? Which Nation?" It says: "The collapse of communism unleashed a hissing snake which has been spitting its venom most caustically among the ruins of the former Yugoslav state. Although the snake sibilation has been heard elsewhere in post-communist Europe, the virulence makes the Yugoslav case the most striking example, not least because the issues involved were most clearly defined there, but because there was another related hissing snake peculiar to the Yugoslav context. Indeed, the particular creature is the prompt for the hissing snake characterisation of the problematics of sovereignty, self-determination, statehood and security - the four S-words which have returned with a vengeance on the European scene but which have significant global echoes." That is strong language, is it not Dr. Gow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know what you mean by -- I am afraid I do not understand what you mean by the term "strong language", but ----

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I am afraid I am not able to express myself more clearly as to what "strong language" is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by "strong language", Dr. Gow would I say, I do not know. He says I cannot say whether it is strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: I thought it was clear, but I have to ask my native speakers. I do agree with my what learned English friends say, that it is emotional language, that through imagery you are painting a picture, that is what is strong language. I do agree. I do understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you are suggesting that it was an attempt at a playful and slightly literary introduction, then I do not think that I could possibly try to say that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: OK. You went further, Dr. Gow. I will read again: "The hissing snake peculiar to the Yugoslav context, the inspirational serpent is that of Serbian nationalism, generated around the four SSSSs which appear on the traditional Serbian symbol which has come to be equated in some eyes with the Nazi swastika." I would like to read another passage to you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Indicate, Mr. Orie, for the record what page you are reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first passage I was reading, your Honour, was page 456, the first paragraph. The second part I was reading was page 457, almost at the bottom, the first lines of "SSSS, the hissing snake of Serbian nationalism". I will read now from page 471. It says at the top of the page: "The reality that Serbia and the Serbs outside its borders provoked the other republics into declaring their independence and initiated the war cannot be overlooked, nor can the reality that without acceptance of the Croatian and Bosnia Herzegovina states by the Serbs living within them, there is a problem of legitimation". You went on, Dr. Gow, and I am now reading from page 475, the first part of the conclusion: "The major question on the international agenda in the wake of collapse in Yugoslavia and the Soviet Union has been to come to terms with the 'Hissing Snake' of questions unleashed by the end of the Cold War; sovereignty, self-determination, statehood and security. The collapse of communism and a need to rebuild states and, in several cases, to build new ones altered the focused on these concepts. Each has had to be addressed with new urgency and has entered a process of reinterpretation. That process has taken place in the light of, in the midst of, and surrounded by, the Yugoslav war of this dissolution. Whilst these issues have not been the only, or even the crucial elements in that war, they have played a major role. "It is plain that a clear understanding of these words-with-two-meanings, including an awareness of their existence, is required before the problems which arise from their ambiguities can be addressed. The possible impact of differing understandings is a attested by the war in Yugoslavia, where the 'Hissing Snake' of Serb nationalism has uncoiled around these issues. The events in Yugoslavia have demonstrated what can happen where these concepts are not clearly understood by either the protagonists or those outside the conflict attempting to deal with it." I finally read to you the very end of the article you have written where it says: "Sovereignty may have to be asserted through the use of armed force - and the use of armed force may be the only way to obtain tame some 'hissing snakes' once they have begun to spit their venom." Dr. Gow, does not your disparaging description of Serbia indicate your prejudice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not -- I am not aware that there is a disparaging description, did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Description of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware that there is any description of Serbia and certainly not that it is disparaging and it does not indicate prejudice of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to ask you, referring to what I said this morning, whether you would grant an adjournment until Monday morning because we have to prepare. We cannot do it all here. We have to find our sources and we need the weekend for that. If you would allow an adjournment?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we can adjourn today, almost an hour early, 15 minutes or thereabouts early. We would normally adjourn at 5.30. So, we will do this, but you understand, as you said earlier before our lunch break, that this this is an exceptional request and it will not be a practice I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. ORIE
utterances.text: It will not be a practice, but the overwhelming material that has been presented and discussed, and apart from that Mr. Kay has not been assisting us for a few days.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That I understand, but the exhibits were exchanged beforehand. The Prosecution did give the Defence all of the exhibits I am sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, last December, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is correct. I might clarify that we had some division in who will prepare what. Here we had the same problem.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand. You have your problems and I guess I have my responsibility. My responsibility is not be too flexible. So I am trying to hold you to the time. Normally we would go to 5.30, but I understand your circumstances. We will adjourn until Monday at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
